title: Accessibility and visuals
note: Written before the Stage 8 sandbox harness ran. It records expected status and method, not observed results. It is not self-approval and makes no release claim. Expected PASS does not override an actual FAIL; any FAIL/BLOCKED is reported as observed.

S8-01.title: Automated accessibility
S8-01.expected: Pinned axe-core 4.11.0 default rules run in Chromium, Firefox, WebKit and mobile Chromium on the default page, and in Chromium on selected-style, clipboard-fallback, source-expanded, narrow-view and JS-asset-blocked states. No serious or critical axe violations. Moderate/minor violations and incomplete results are reported, not hidden. Negative controls with a missing label and low-contrast text are detected by the same scanner. The pre-existing Q-002 missing-JS-asset failure state remains OPEN and is not waived by any S8 result.

S8-02.title: Keyboard operation
S8-02.expected: Real Tab and Shift+Tab traversal reaches every focusable control in logical DOM order exactly once, with visible focus and no focus trap. Enter/Space operate the skip link, text inputs, native size select, copy, download, every style button and details summaries. Focus is never moved into a control programmatically to manufacture a keyboard claim; programmatic focus only occurs as the product's documented clipboard-fallback behaviour. External production links are focused and their hrefs checked but not activated to avoid network.

S8-03.title: Labels and roles
S8-03.expected: Every interactive control has a non-empty accessible name and the expected role/state. The size select is named 'Size' and does not absorb its option text. The preview has role img and an updating accessible label; generated decorative SVG and gallery thumbnails are hidden from assistive technology. State buttons expose aria-pressed. The static HTML with the JS asset blocked still labels seed, name, size and both textareas.

S8-04.title: Status announcements
S8-04.expected: One live DOM status region has role=status and aria-live=polite. Copy success, clipboard fallback/failure and download success set the fixed visible messages and do not duplicate the live region. Render updates clear the status without noisy announcements. No screen-reader speech verification is claimed because no assistive technology is available; that manual subcheck is BLOCKED. A synthetic download-exception probe is recorded as an explicit limitation, not a speech claim. Q-002 remains OPEN and is not waived.

S8-05.title: Zoom and reflow
S8-05.expected: Using Chromium CDP device metrics, a 1280 CSS-px reference becomes 640 and 320 CSS-px layout viewports for 200% and 400% layout equivalence. This is documented as layout-viewport equivalence, not a claim of browser page-zoom visual scaling; a separate pinch-zoom emulation is recorded only as non-reflow. At 200% and 400% equivalents there is no horizontal page overflow or hidden content/control loss and every control remains keyboard-reachable. A synthetic 200% text-only enlargement stress test is also run and its method/limits are stated. Firefox and WebKit are checked at 320 CSS px for narrow reflow.

S8-06.title: Mobile and visual inspection
S8-06.expected: Chromium at 360x800, 360x640, 390x844, 844x390, 768x1024, 1024x768 and desktop 1280x800 is measured. Primary targets are preferably 44x44 CSS px; WCAG 2.2 minimum 24x24 or the spacing/inline exceptions are applied with actual bounding boxes. All eight styles are selected at 192 px on a 360 px viewport without clipping. Long-source clipboard fallback and a keyboard-overlay emulation (explicitly emulation-only) are inspected. Screenshots are captured and visually inspected after retrieval, not treated as pixel baselines.

S8-07.title: Contrast and forced colors
S8-07.expected: Computed WCAG AA checks require 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text. Control boundaries and focus indicators require 3:1 against the adjacent background; selected state must not rely on colour alone and must expose aria-pressed. Text, control boundaries, focus and selected state are measured from actual computed colours and inspected in screenshots. Chromium forced-colors emulation is checked for visible boundaries, focus and selected state without colour alone. A synthetic low-contrast negative control must be detected by the same checker. If any required ratio is unmet, the scenario is FAIL and is not waived.

S8-08.title: Reduced motion
S8-08.expected: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce emulated in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, computed animation-name, animation-duration and transition-duration show no non-essential animation on any element or pseudo-element. The no-preference baseline is compared; the page is not required to invent an animation to suppress.

S8-09.title: Native Safari
S8-09.expected: Remains BLOCKED. The sandbox is Linux and provides Playwright WebKit, which is not macOS Safari and is not a substitute. No native Safari PASS is claimed or waived; WebKit results are supplementary only.

axe.moderateMinor: reported with rule ids, impact, targets and assessment

contrast.largeTextDefinition: >=24 px normal weight or >=18.66 px bold

required: the same axe scanner detects a missing accessible name and low-contrast text on a bounded disposable page
the same keyboard focus checker detects a bounded disposable page whose controls suppress visible focus
the same contrast checker detects the low-contrast text and passes the real page text
clean controls pass the axe and focus checks

Q-002.rule: Blocking the site JavaScript asset with scripting enabled leaves static content readable but the playground has no explanatory failure state. Stage 8 records the reproduction and does not fix or waive it.

S7-WebKit-CSP.status: attribution recorded in S7 evidence; do not blanket-ignore violations
S7-WebKit-CSP.rule: The known WebKit 27.2 style-src-attr warning is expected only from the native select while select function still works. Any other CSP violation is reported, not suppressed, and CSP is not weakened. Playwright/web-inspector screenshot style injection is attributed separately.

environment.browsers: Chromium, Firefox, WebKit and mobile Chromium via pinned @playwright/test 1.64.1
environment.site: actual tracked site built in sandbox with root npm ci and npm run build:site
